attrs.why: Radiologist analysis notes dermoscopy shows translucent epidermis, branched vessels, and marginal hair bulbs, and head CT shows no osseous, vascular, neural, or soft-tissue defects; these findings support a chronic congenital/atrophic scalp anomaly and argue against acute infection or neoplasm. Combined with lifelong stable alopecic patches since birth and an atrophic boggy scalp lesion, confidence increases from 0.55 to 0.75.

New dermoscopy and head CT findings (translucent epidermis, branched vessels, marginal hair bulbs; no soft-tissue defect or mass) argue against acute infection or inflammation, and the lifelong stable asymptomatic alopecia lacks acute signs. Confidence decreases from 0.35 to 0.10.
New dermoscopy and head CT findings show no neoplastic/adnexal features or soft-tissue mass; lifelong stability further refutes an aggressive neoplasm. Confidence decreases from 0.2 to 0.05.

New structural scalp findings (atrophic patch, dermoscopy abnormalities) support a congenital/atrophic anomaly rather than isolated primary neuralgia; the pain is better explained by the structural scalp defect. Confidence decreases from 0.1 to 0.05.

attrs.why: Dermoscopy findings of translucent epidermis, branched vessels, and marginal hair bulbs, together with head CT showing no underlying osseous/vascular/neural/soft-tissue defects, support a congenital atrophic scalp anomaly. Combined with lifelong stable alopecic patches since birth, this specific congenital scalp defect is favored. Confidence is 0.55 because birth records/MRI are missing and the recent tenderness is atypical.
